title: Apache Iceberg vs Delta Lake Comparison
summary: A 2026 comparison of Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake table formats, covering their differing metadata architectures, the two formats' recent convergence efforts, and how OneLake exposes cross-format interoperability for Fabric lakehouses.
audience: Data engineers and architects evaluating open table format choices, particularly those weighing Fabric lakehouse/OneLake against multi-engine lakehouse stacks built on Iceberg.
why_it_matters: Table-format interoperability determines whether a Fabric lakehouse can participate in a multi-engine data estate without duplicating data; understanding OneLake's Iceberg support clarifies when Fabric can sit alongside Databricks, Snowflake, or open-catalog architectures rather than requiring a rip-and-replace.
takeaways: Iceberg and Delta Lake both write data as Parquet but track table state through different metadata mechanisms, which is why cross-format reads require translation rather than being trivial.
OneLake provides three distinct mechanisms for Iceberg interoperability, not just one, each suited to different integration scenarios.

Fabric lakehouses remain natively Delta-format, so Iceberg support is about letting external engines and Iceberg-native tables interoperate with OneLake, not a format change for Fabric-created tables.
The broader ecosystem (Delta UniForm, Iceberg v3) is converging toward mutual readability, which reduces the cost of picking either format as a starting point.

claims.text: OneLake exposes an Iceberg REST Catalog API so that external query engines can address Fabric-resident tables using standard Iceberg catalog connection strings.
OneLake supports table format virtualization, presenting a Delta table's metadata as Iceberg-readable (and vice versa) without physically rewriting the underlying Parquet data.
OneLake Shortcuts can point a Fabric Lakehouse at externally-hosted Iceberg tables stored in S3 or ADLS Gen2, per the post.
Fabric lakehouses are described as a natural fit for Delta Lake workloads because Fabric lakehouse tables are natively Delta-formatted rather than Iceberg.
Iceberg and Delta Lake both persist actual row data as ordinary Parquet files on object storage; the formats differ only in how they track table metadata and snapshot history.

Iceberg organizes table state as a tree of snapshots pointing to manifest lists and manifest files, coordinated through an external catalog, whereas Delta Lake uses a self-describing append-only JSON transaction log with periodic Parquet checkpoints and does not require an external catalog to read current state.
Delta UniForm lets a single copy of Delta table data be read as an Iceberg table by external engines such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Trino, and Dremio, avoiding a second data copy.
